title: Local and global algebraic-space dimension from etale scheme charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $F$ a presheaf of sets on schemes over $S$, with the universe convention of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use its field-valued point classes $|F|$ and maps $|a|$ from [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. For $x\in|F|$, define $d_x(F)=\sup\{\dim_t(T): a:h_T\to F\text{ is representable etale},\ t\in T,\ |a|(t)=x\}$, where representable etale has the scheme-test meaning of [def-trf-algebraic-space] and $\dim_t(T)$ is the infimum of Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods from [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Define $d(F)=\sup_{x\in|F|}d_x(F)$, with values in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$ and empty supremum $-\infty$. For an algebraic space, every point has a chart and all the chart values agree, so these formulas are the usual local and global dimension $\dim_x(F)$ and $\dim F$.

source.place: definition-dimension-at-point and definition-dimension, with the etale-descent independence of the chart explained immediately before definition-dimension-at-point. Supremum over all chart values is the choice-free construction of their common value.
